cards.front: Why does replacing a nested scan with a Hash Map drop Two-Sum from O(n²) to O(n)?
cards.hint: Trade O(n) auxiliary memory for O(1) complement lookup
cards.back: Each element x checks `seen.has(target - x)` in average O(1) time instead of scanning the remaining n elements.

cards.front: When should you reach for the Sliding Window pattern?
cards.back: Whenever you need the longest, shortest, or optimal contiguous range in an array/string without re-scanning interior items.
cards.example: Expand `right` every step; shrink `left` in a `while` loop when the window violates the invariant. Each index enters and exits once → O(n).

cards.front: Binary search beyond sorted arrays: what is 'Binary Search on the Answer'?
cards.hint: Think monotonic predicate ok(mid): false, false, true, true
cards.back: If feasibility flips monotonically from false to true across [lo, hi], binary search finds the exact threshold in O(log R · cost(ok)).
cards.example: Use `mid = lo + Math.floor((hi - lo) / 2)` to prevent overflow and converge cleanly on the first `true`.

cards.front: How do you maintain the top-K largest items in an unbounded stream?
cards.hint: Counter-intuitive: use a MIN-heap, not a max-heap
cards.back: Keep a min-heap of size K. The root is the K-th largest; push only when x > root and pop the smallest in O(log K).
cards.example: Time: O(n log K), Space: O(K) — dramatically faster than sorting the full stream O(n log n).

cards.front: BFS vs. DFS vs. Dijkstra: which finds the shortest path?
cards.hint: Check whether edge weights exist and whether any are negative
cards.back: BFS for unweighted graphs O(V+E); Dijkstra (min-heap) for non-negative weights O((V+E) log V); DFS does not guarantee shortest paths.
cards.example: 0-1 weighted graph shortcut: use a deque (0-1 BFS) in linear O(V+E) time.

cards.front: What are the 3 ingredients of every Dynamic Programming solution?
cards.back: 1) Minimal state describing a subproblem, 2) Recurrence linking smaller states, 3) Base cases + topological evaluation order.
cards.example: Start with clean recursion + memoization; optimize to bottom-up rolling variables when `dp[i]` depends only on `dp[i-1]`.

cards.front: What does 'Make illegal states unrepresentable' mean in practice?
cards.hint: Replace loose booleans/nullables with discriminated unions or sealed classes
cards.back: Encode domain states in the type system so contradictory flags (e.g., `loading=true` AND `error!=null`) cannot compile.
cards.example: Kotlin: `sealed interface UiState { object Loading; data class Ready(val data: T); data class Failed(val msg: String) }`

cards.front: What is Idempotency, and why do retryable APIs depend on it?
cards.hint: f(f(x)) = f(x) even after a network timeout
cards.back: An operation is idempotent if executing it multiple times with the same key produces the same side effect as executing it once.
cards.example: Attach a client-generated `Idempotency-Key` UUID so safe retries never double-charge or duplicate records.

cards.front: Debounce vs. Throttle: when do you pick each?
cards.hint: Wait for silence vs. pace a steady heartbeat
cards.back: Debounce fires once after input pauses for N ms (search box). Throttle fires at most once every N ms (scroll, sensor sampling).
cards.example: MindLoop uses debounced writes for mood notes and throttled sampling for live accelerometer step detection.

cards.front: Why does column order matter in a composite SQL index `(user_id, created_at)`?
cards.hint: Leftmost prefix rule in a B-Tree
cards.back: B-Trees sort by `user_id` first, then `created_at` within each user. Queries filtering only `created_at` cannot seek the prefix.
cards.example: Rule of thumb: put exact-equality columns first, then the range or `ORDER BY` column.

cards.front: Why enable WAL (Write-Ahead Logging) mode in offline SQLite apps?
cards.hint: Readers don't block writers; writers don't block readers
cards.back: WAL appends changes to a sequential log file, allowing concurrent UI reads and fast atomic commits on mobile flash storage.
cards.example: Before exporting a single `.sqlite` backup file, run `PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(FULL)` to flush all pages cleanly.

cards.front: Why add random jitter to exponential backoff?
cards.hint: Prevent the 'thundering herd' after an outage
cards.back: Without jitter, thousands of clients synchronize their retry intervals and hammer the recovering service at the exact same millisecond.
